newsitem.title: INDIA: India's STC says bought 1.74 mln t wheat since Dec.
newsitem.headline: India's STC says bought 1.74 mln t wheat since Dec.

text.p: India's State Trading Corporation (STC) said on Friday that since December it has purchased 1.74 million tonnes of wheat out of two million tonnes authorised by the government.

A report by the U.S. agricultural attache released in Washington on Thursday said India recently bought 1.0 million tonnes of Australian wheat, bringing its combined purchases since December to nearly 2.7 million tonnes.
Asked to comment on the U.S. report, a senior STC official said: "I am not aware of it. I have done 1.74 million, and that's where we stand."
The official, who asked not to be identified, said STC had a mandate to import two million tonnes.
"I have done only 1.74 million. I am still aiming to cover the remaining," he said. "We are still negotiating. Meetings are still going on."
In March STC tendered for 50,000 tonnes of wheat imports for arrivals in the post-monsoon season from September onwards. The tenders closed on March 25.
"The tender that we floated for 50,000 tonnes is still continuing. Various formulas are being discussed," the official said, indicating that no fresh deals had been made.
The official said there was obviously a lot of speculation in the market on purchases by STC.
"We are not able to get good prices. Discussions are on and I am in no position to say how it will end," the official said. "We are going on with fresh quotes."
STC made its previous purchases mainly from Australia, Canada and Argentina.
